title: Roots-of-unity comparison: transition compatibility and isomorphism along isomorphisms
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and for $N\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ let $c^f_{\mu_N}:f^{-1}\mu_{N,Y}\to\mu_{N,X}$ be the inverse-image comparison map of the pro-etale sheaves of $N$-th roots of unity [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image, def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], and $c^f_{\mathbf Z/N}:f^{-1}(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)_Y\to(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)_X$ the structure map of constant sheaves [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then:

1. For $N\mid N'$ and the transition maps $t_{N',N}:u\mapsto u^{N'/N}$ of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], $t_{N',N}\circ c^f_{\mu_{N'}}=c^f_{\mu_N}\circ f^{-1}(t_{N',N})$; so for a prime $\ell$ the maps $c^f_{\mu_{\ell^r}}$, $r\geq1$, form a morphism of inverse systems $(f^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,Y})_r\to(\mu_{\ell^r,X})_r$.
2. $c^f_{\mu_N}$ is semilinear over $c^f_{\mathbf Z/N}$: $c^f_{\mu_N}(a\cdot u)=c^f_{\mathbf Z/N}(a)\cdot c^f_{\mu_N}(u)$ for local sections $a$ of $f^{-1}(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)_Y$ and $u$ of $f^{-1}\mu_{N,Y}$, the module structures being those of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf].
3. If $f$ is an isomorphism of schemes, then $c^f_{\mu_N}$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of abelian groups; under the identification $(f^{-1}\mathcal F)(U\xrightarrow{u}X)\cong\mathcal F(U\xrightarrow{f\circ u}Y)$ of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (1) it is the identity of $\{v\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:v^N=1\}$.

source.place: (2.2), pp. 280-281 (transition maps x -> x^l of the system Z/l^n(1)); the compatibilities are written out by the worker

proof.text:
Write $\beta^f_M:\mu_{M,Y}\to f_*\mu_{M,X}$ for the map whose adjoint is $c^f_{\mu_M}$. Put $k=N'/N$, an integer since $N\mid N'$. For every $V\to Y$ and $v\in\mu_{N',Y}(V)$ the ring map on global sections gives
$$\beta^f_N(V)(v^k)=\mathrm{pr}_V^\sharp(v^k)=\bigl(\mathrm{pr}_V^\sharp v\bigr)^k.$$
These are sections of $\mu_{N,X}(X\times_YV)$: their $N$-th powers are $1$, since $kN=N'$. Thus equality on all sections gives the sheaf-map identity
$$f_*(t^X_{N',N})\circ\beta^f_{N'}=\beta^f_N\circ t^Y_{N',N}.$$
Here the restrictions and the transition maps are exactly those in the two roots-of-unity definitions, not transitions of constant sheaves.

proof.text: The adjunction $L=f^{-1}\dashv R=f_*$ sends a map $a:L\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ to $R(a)\circ\eta_{\mathcal F}$. For $a=t^X_{N',N}\circ c^f_{\mu_{N'}}$ its image is $R(t^X_{N',N})\circ\beta^f_{N'}$. For $b=c^f_{\mu_N}\circ L(t^Y_{N',N})$ its image is $\beta^f_N\circ t^Y_{N',N}$, because $RL(t^Y_{N',N})\circ\eta_{\mu_{N',Y}}=\eta_{\mu_{N,Y}}\circ t^Y_{N',N}$. Step 1 equates these images, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives clause 1. Taking $N=\ell^r$ and $N'=\ell^{r+1}$ makes each square of the two inverse systems commute; hence these comparisons form the asserted morphism of inverse systems.

source.place: Tag 00WX, lemma-adjoint-sheaves; naturality and injectivity of the defining adjunction, applied to step 1

proof.text: For clause 2 put $R_Y=(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)_Y$, $R_X=(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)_X$, $A=f^{-1}R_Y$, $H=f^{-1}\mu_{N,Y}$, and $G=\mu_{N,X}$. The inverse-image construction supplies the stated $A$-module structure on $H$. Apply the constant-ring comparison proposition to the finite discrete commutative ring $\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$: it says exactly that the structure map $c=c^f_{\mathbf Z/N}:A\to R_X$ used here is an isomorphism. Let $q=c^{-1}$. Give $H$ an $R_X$-action by $b\star h=q(b)\cdot h$. The ring-map and module axioms verify the module axioms for $\star$, and restriction compatibility follows from that of $q$ and the original action. Since $q$ is unital, for every integer $m$ the constant class $\overline m$ acts by $q(\overline m)=m1_A$, hence by $mh$ in the underlying abelian group. In particular $Nh=0$, because $\overline N=0$. These statements hold over every object, including the empty object and when $N=1$.

source.place: Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf, and proetale.tex Tag 09A5, section-morphism; constant-ring comparison is the existing proposition, while restriction of scalars is checked explicitly

proof.text:
The torsion-sheaf lemma (1) identifies the $R_X$-module structure $\star$ from step 3 with the unique constant-coefficient structure on the $N$-torsion abelian sheaf $H$, because its constant sections act by integer representatives. The same lemma identifies the module structure on $G$ from the roots-of-unity definition. The comparison $c^f_{\mu_N}:H\to G$ is already a morphism of abelian sheaves by its definition, so part (2) of that lemma makes it $R_X$-linear for $\star$. For local sections $a\in A(U)$ and $h\in H(U)$ substitute $b=c(a)$ and use $q(c(a))=a$ to obtain
$$c^f_{\mu_N}(a\cdot h)=c^f_{\mu_N}(c(a)\star h)=c(a)\cdot c^f_{\mu_N}(h).$$
This proves clause 2 for all local sections of the inverse-image ring, rather than only the constant ones.

proof.text: Now assume $f$ is an isomorphism. The site-isomorphism lemma (1) says that $\Phi_f(U\xrightarrow{u}X)=(U\xrightarrow{fu}Y)$ is a covering-preserving equivalence and describes inverse image by this change of structure map. To fix its canonical normalization, use the comma-category construction of inverse image. For $U\to X$ let $V_0=(U\xrightarrow{fu}Y)$ and $\gamma=(u,\mathrm{id}_U):U\to X\times_Y V_0$. The pair $(V_0,\gamma)$ is initial in $\mathcal I_U$: for $(V,\phi)$ the unique possible map $V_0\to V$ is $h=\mathrm{pr}_V\phi$, and $(\mathrm{id}_X\times_Yh)\gamma=\phi$ because both projections agree. Uniqueness follows by composing this equality with $\mathrm{pr}_V$. Thus it is terminal in $\mathcal I_U^{\mathrm{op}}$. Explicitly the maps $\mathcal F(V)\xrightarrow{\mathcal F(h)}\mathcal F(V_0)$ form a cocone, and its map from the colimit is inverse to the coprojection from $\mathcal F(V_0)$: one composite is the identity at $V_0$, and the other is the identity on every coprojection by the cocone relation. This identifies $u_{f,p}\mathcal F(U)$ with $\mathcal F(V_0)$, naturally in $U$. For a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ over $X$, the covering $\{\Phi_f(U_i)\to\Phi_f(U)\}$ over $Y$ has the same underlying schemes and overlap schemes. Thus a matching family for $U\mapsto\mathcal F(\Phi_f(U))$ is exactly a matching family for $\mathcal F$ on that covering; its unique gluing proves that this presheaf is a sheaf. The sheafification universal property therefore leaves it unchanged. This is precisely the canonical identification in clause 3.

proof.text:
For an arbitrary $(V,\phi)$ the presheaf map adjoint to $\beta^f_N$ sends the coprojection of $v\in\mu_{N,Y}(V)$ to $\phi^\sharp(\mathrm{pr}_V^\sharp v)$. Indeed, for an arrow $a:(V,\phi)\to(V^{\prime},\phi^{\prime})$ of $\mathcal I_U$ we have $\phi^{\prime}=(\mathrm{id}_X\times_Ya)\phi$, so for $v^{\prime}\in\mu_{N,Y}(V^{\prime})$ functoriality gives $\phi^{\prime\sharp}\mathrm{pr}_{V^{\prime}}^\sharp(v^{\prime})=\phi^\sharp\mathrm{pr}_V^\sharp(a^\sharp v^{\prime})$, the required cocone relation. Restriction along $b:U^{\prime}\to U$ gives $(\phi b)^\sharp\mathrm{pr}_V^\sharp(v)=b^\sharp\phi^\sharp\mathrm{pr}_V^\sharp(v)$, proving naturality in $U$. On $U=X\times_YV$, $\phi=\mathrm{id}$ the formula recovers $\beta^f_N(V)$; this verifies its adjunction characterization. They extend uniquely through sheafification. At the distinguished pair $(V_0,\gamma)$ of step 5, this value is
$$\gamma^\sharp\mathrm{pr}_{V_0}^\sharp(v)=(\mathrm{pr}_{V_0}\gamma)^\sharp(v)=v,$$
since $\mathrm{pr}_{V_0}\gamma=\mathrm{id}_U$. The coprojection at this pair is the inverse of the identification in step 5, so $c^f_{\mu_N}(U)$ is the identity on $\{v\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:v^N=1\}$ under that identification. These identities are natural in $U$ and give inverse sheaf morphisms; hence $c^f_{\mu_N}$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. This proves every assertion of clause 3 without choosing a root of unity or assuming that $N$ is invertible on $X$.
